verses.text: At that time, Jesus was walking through grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry, so they picked heads of grain and ate.
When the Pharisees saw it, they said to him, “Look, your disciples are doing something the Law doesn’t allow on the Sabbath.”
He replied, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
He went into God’s house and ate the sacred bread. It wasn’t lawful for him or his companions to eat it; only the priests could.
Or haven’t you read in the Law that the priests in the temple work on the Sabbath and are still innocent?
I tell you, someone greater than the temple is here.
If you understood what this means—‘I want mercy, not sacrifice’—you wouldn’t have condemned innocent people.
The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Jesus left there and went into their synagogue.
A man with a disabled hand was there. The Pharisees asked Jesus, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” They were looking for a reason to accuse him.
He answered, “If one of you has a sheep that falls into a pit on the Sabbath, won’t you grab it and pull it out?
A person is worth so much more than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”
Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” The man stretched it out, and it was restored, just like his other hand.
But the Pharisees left and plotted how they could destroy Jesus.
Jesus knew this and withdrew from there. Large crowds followed him, and he healed them all.
He warned them not to tell people who he was.
This fulfilled what God had spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
“Here is my servant, whom I chose, the one I love and delight in. I’ll put my Spirit on him, and he’ll announce justice to the nations.
He won’t argue or shout, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
He won’t break a bruised reed or put out a smoldering wick, until he leads justice to victory.
The nations will put their hope in his name.”
Then someone brought Jesus a demon-possessed man who was blind and couldn’t speak. Jesus healed him, and the man could speak and see.
All the crowds were amazed and asked, “Could this be the Son of David?”
When the Pharisees heard this, they said, “This man only drives out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of demons.”
Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be destroyed, and no city or household divided against itself will stand.
If Satan drives out Satan, he’s fighting against himself. How could his kingdom stand?
If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, who gives your own people power to drive them out? They’ll be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by God’s Spirit, then God’s Kingdom has already come upon you.
How can anyone enter a strong man’s house and take his belongings unless they first tie him up? Then they can plunder his house.
“Whoever isn’t with me is against me, and whoever doesn’t gather with me scatters.
So I tell you, every sin and insult against God can be forgiven, but insulting the Spirit will not be forgiven.
Whoever speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit won’t be forgiven, either in this age or the age to come.
“Make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad. A tree is recognized by its fruit.
You brood of snakes! How can you, being evil, say anything good? The mouth speaks from whatever fills the heart.
A good person brings good things out of a good store of the heart; an evil person brings evil things out of an evil store.
I tell you, on judgment day people will have to answer for every careless word they speak.
Your words will either show you’re right or condemn you.”
Then some scribes and Pharisees answered him, “Teacher, we want you to show us a sign.”
He replied, “An evil and unfaithful generation keeps demanding a sign, but the only sign it will be given is the sign of the prophet Jonah.
Just as Jonah spent three days and three nights inside the huge fish, the Son of Man will spend three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
The people of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it. They turned back to God when Jonah preached, and now someone greater than Jonah is here.
The Queen of the South will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it. She came from far away to hear Solomon’s wisdom, and now someone greater than Solomon is here.
“When an unclean spirit leaves a person, it travels through dry places looking for somewhere to rest but finds none.
Then it says, ‘I’ll go back to the house I left.’ It returns and finds the house empty, swept clean, and put in order.
Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they all move in. That person’s final condition is worse than before. That’s how it will be with this evil generation.”
While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak with him.
Someone told him, “Look, your mother and brothers are outside, asking to speak with you.”
He answered the person, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
He pointed toward his disciples and said, “Look, here are my mother and brothers!
Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother, sister, and mother.”
